Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I5 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires an explicit whole-brain users-vs-controls GM contrast (I3), this study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heavy smokers (n=16) to matched non-smoker controls and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates. The paper provides between-group GM contrasts (VBM) and reports MNI coordinates for GM reductions in bilateral cerebellar tonsil (with small-volume correction) and describes whole-brain thresholding procedures; demographic, substance-use (cigarettes/day, years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PROBID for SVM) are reported. Voxelwise results are given in-text with coordinates and figures. Although some GM results are reported with small-volume correction, the study conducted whole-brain VBM and provides qualifying voxelwise results; therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5/E6).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine (stimulant) users and controls (meets I2). It reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (meets I5). However, the primary voxelwise analyses are within the abstinent cocaine group (regressions of GM against weeks abstinent and years of use). The paper does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group (substance users vs controls) contrast; comparisons to controls were performed post-hoc on extracted ROIs (Welch t-tests), i.e. ROI-based tests rather than a qualifying whole-brain between-group analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (combined voxel-wise P<0.001 and cluster-extent thresholds with PFWE<0.05), provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes in results/tables and figures, and describes participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (VBM8, SPM8). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (including cluster coordinates, sizes and corrected p-values) and a between-group contrast (controls > CUD) for the mid-cingulate cortex, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, and it is empirical human MRI work). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusions.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing treatment-naive alcohol-dependent individuals (n=24) to controls (n=17). It reports whole-brain measures (total cortical gray matter differences) and regional cortical gray matter volume differences (prefrontal and parietal regions) between groups, acquired on a 1.5T scanner with detailed preprocessing and statistical methods described. Participant demographics (male, ages described), substance use characteristics (lifetime duration, consumption), MRI field strength, and software/statistics (SAS PROC GLM) are reported. The study is not ROI-only (it includes whole-brain total cortical gray matter contrasts and regional analyses mapped in the Talairach system), so it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons and provides usable regional results relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The Methods and Results describe whole-brain VBM analyses (ANCOVA, DARTEL normalization, modulation) with reported widespread GM reductions in ADP versus HC (reported in main text and Supporting Information tables), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant demographics (age range, sex matching), substance-use measures (LDH, craving, days abstinent, relapse classification), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; empirical human structural MRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing whole-brain gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls. The Methods report a whole-brain between-groups VBM analysis with results (greater GM volume in right caudate and right orbitofrontal gyri) presented in figures/tables. MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical approaches are described (with supporting information). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group VBM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use details, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics provided). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group SnPM VBM results (significant clusters in right frontal lobe) and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results and coordinates are described/mentioned. Participant demographics (male, ages reported), substance-use characteristics (SC use duration and detected compounds listed in appendix), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SnPM) are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, limitations, appendix). Therefore include for meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs. controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing substance users (alcohol, cocaine, and/or cannabis dependence) with healthy controls and reported between-group whole-brain GMV contrasts (cluster coordinates, figures, and ROI volume estimates). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are provided. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing grey matter between alcohol users and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster-corrected results and provides coordinate-based correlational analyses. Key study details are reported: participant demographics (age range, all male), substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol abuse, years and amount of use), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5, detailed pipeline). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) performed at 3.0 T that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of grey matter volumes between alcohol use disorder (AUD) participants and healthy controls, and also reports comparisons involving problem gamblers. The methods section describes MRI acquisition, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), statistical analysis (whole-brain FDR correction), and participant demographics (male-only sample, ages, AUDIT scores, abstinence duration, smoking status), satisfying reporting expectations. The paper clearly provides whole-brain voxelwise results (significant clusters reported and visualized) comparing substance users (alcohol) vs controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and matched controls. The full text provides introduction, detailed methods (participants, 3T MRI acquisition, SPM8 VBM/DARTEL preprocessing, AFNI statistical analyses), results of whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (with cluster-corrected significance, figures and tables), and discussion. Substance use characteristics, participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not a review). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs CON) with voxelwise results presented in tables and figures, specifies MRI field strength (4 Tesla), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and provides participant demographics (male, ages) and detailed substance-use characteristics (years of cocaine, alcohol, smoking). The study is not ROI-only and contains original data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users and matched healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise VBM analyses (whole-brain processing described) and presents between-group contrasts with coordinates (referenced Tables/Figures) showing reduced VMPFC gray matter in CUD (ROI-corrected FWE) and notes whole-brain results (no other clusters survived whole-brain correction). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without whole-brain analyses; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that compares gray matter between 20 alcohol-dependent patients and 20 controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts using SPM2 with thresholding and describes significant clusters/regions (tables/figures). Participant characteristics (male, age-matched), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants (n=130) with healthy controls (n=69) using whole-brain vertex-wise (node-to-node) cortical thickness analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (alcoholics vs. controls and sex-specific contrasts), regional results with coordinates/effect sizes, and relevant participant and MRI details (age/sex, substance use characteristics, 1.5T field strength, FreeSurfer processing, AFNI/SUMA statistics). Although the metric is cortical thickness rather than voxel-based GM volume/density, cortical thickness is a valid whole-brain structural grey-matter measure relevant to the review objective of identifying structural GM alterations in substance users. The study is not ROI-only and is empirical with original human MRI data, so it meets the inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM structural comparisons.

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing gray matter volume between cocaine use disorder (CUD) participants and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain 2 (Diagnosis) × 2 (PENK) ANCOVA VBM results with cluster-corrected thresholds and identifies a significant Diagnosis × PENK interaction in right inferior frontal gyrus gray matter volume, indicating whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM differences. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8), and substance-use/sample characteristics and demographic covariates are described in the methods. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM group comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I5 (reporting of key methodological/participant details) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey-matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM/2-sample t-test) and reporting voxelwise regression results. The paper reports whole-brain GM between-group contrasts (FDR-corrected clusters) and voxelwise longitudinal Jacobian analyses, with results presented in text and figures. Participant demographics (n, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5, SPM5, TBM methods) are described or referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM structural comparisons in alcohol users versus controls.

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study directly comparing smokers (nicotine users) and nonsmoking controls. The study used whole-brain coverage via a 1,024-ROI parcellation of the AAL atlas, performed VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data, and applied multivariate classification to discriminate groups. Results include a map of consistent ROIs (N=150) and a table (Table 2) that lists ROIs with MNI center coordinates and sizes, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise/coordinate results be available. Participant demographics, smoking measures (FTND, CPD, lifetime usage), scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary analysis is a multivariate classifier rather than a conventional univariate voxelwise t-contrast, the paper provides whole-brain-derived regional results with coordinates and regression analyses relating GMV to smoking measures, which meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; I5 (reporting details) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using VBM (modulated GM segments) to compare alcohol-dependent patients (n=19) with healthy controls (n=20). It performs voxel-wise analyses (one-sample and between-group two-sample t-tests) of an asymmetry index derived from whole-brain GM maps (processed with SPM8/VBM8 and DARTEL) and reports cluster results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (daily intake, dependence duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses and voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided (within a right-hemispheric gray matter mask) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for empirical whole-brain voxelwise GM analyses comparing substance users (alcohol) and controls and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (SPM8/DARTEL). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster results, MNI/Talairach coordinates, figures, and ROC analyses (satisfying voxelwise reporting). Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition (high-resolution T1 parameters), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; it's original human MRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (regions of decreased grey matter volume in alcoholics) with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics, and provides participant demographics (male-only sample, ages), substance-use characteristics (duration, amount, abstinence), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM). Results are reported voxelwise in the main text/figures and regression analyses were performed; this is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, conclusion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between heroin-dependent patients on methadone maintenance (n=27) and healthy controls (n=23). The paper reports whole-brain VBM between-group contrasts (SPM5/VBM5 with DARTEL), details MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant demographics and substance-use characteristics. Results list regional whole-brain GMV differences and report correlations; coordinate-based voxelwise results are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be included.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume/density between smokers and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM2; FDR-corrected results) with results presented in tables/figures and describes participant demographics (age/sex), smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=95) to healthy controls (n=87) using voxel-based morphometry. The authors report whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (2-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) with reported coordinates and clusters, and also present ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly available. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol dependence, days abstinent), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain VBM voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected) with cluster results presented in figures/tables, and describes participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing smokers and age-matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs non-smokers) with AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise results and region coordinates/tables referenced, and also reports correlations with lifetime tobacco consumption (pack-years). Participant characteristics (all male, ages 23–40), substance-use measures (cigarettes/day, years, pack-years, light vs heavy groups), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Thus it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I4 (results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (key methodological/participant details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine use disorder comparing users and controls (I2 satisfied). However, the manuscript does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls; group comparisons were conducted using predefined bilateral rACC ROIs and ROI-based VBM, and the authors explicitly state they did not perform whole-brain group difference analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users versus controls that performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). However, the paper reports that whole-brain VBM between-group analyses were nonsignificant and therefore provides no qualifying whole-brain coordinates of GM differences; instead, the authors conducted post-hoc ROI analyses (based on fMRI peaks) and report an rACC ROI effect. Because there are no significant whole-brain GM between-group results to include and the reported structural finding is ROI-based, this meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast with significant peaks). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent subjects (including subgroups: ‘pure’ alcoholics and polysubstance-abusing alcoholics) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with permutation-based nonparametric testing and displays/describes significant voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM v1.1, BET, FAST, FLIRT, FNIRT) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing smokers (nicotine users) to never-smokers. Although the paper uses surface-based cortical thickness (rather than VBM-derived volume/density), cortical thickness is a structural grey-matter metric relevant to the review objective of structurally altered GM. The study performs a whole-brain, surface-based between-group analysis (with permutation cluster correction) and reports a surviving cluster in left mOFC with Talairach coordinates and effect size. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), smoking measures (cigarettes/day, pack-years), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical data present). Therefore it meets the inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (two-sample t-tests) with voxelwise results (peaks plotted in MNI space, clusters reported and discussed) rather than ROI-only analyses. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5/SPM5), and participant demographics (age, sex distribution) and substance-use characteristics are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing regular cannabis users and occasional users (controls). Methods report whole-brain two-sample voxelwise contrasts with SPM8, DARTEL registration, modulation, smoothing, and FWE-corrected statistics; results report significant between-group whole-brain clusters (coordinates and cluster descriptions) and voxelwise correlations with usage frequency. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons relevant to cannabis.

The study is empirical, in English, and uses whole-brain voxelwise MRI analyses, but it does NOT report whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead it reports continuous associations between alcohol/cannabis use (AUDIT score, TLFB days) and GM/WM measures in pooled cross-sectional samples. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I2 (requires between-group comparisons of users vs controls) and I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast). It does satisfy I4 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in figures/tables) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance measures, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract this is an empirical 1.5T MRI study reporting gray matter volume deficits in alcoholic patients vs controls, so I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) is met. However, I cannot confirm whether at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (I3) is reported, nor whether coordinate tables/figures for voxelwise results are available (I4). Reporting of participant details and preprocessing/software is incomplete in the abstract (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is not available to verify whole-brain results and requisite detail, I must exclude this study pending access to the complete article.

This study is empirical, in English, uses VBM whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports necessary participant/MRI/preprocessing details, but it does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. Instead, the paper presents whole-brain regression analyses relating number/amount of substances to GM volume across a combined sample. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

The study is excluded because the VBM analyses reported were performed using region-of-interest (ROI) masks derived from the AAL atlas (left lateral frontal, parietal, temporal lobes, hippocampus) rather than reporting a whole-brain between-group (AUD vs. control) voxelwise contrast meeting the review’s whole-brain requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates are reported/quoted in the text/tables), and I5 (participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no clear whole-brain between-group contrast reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete and contains background, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing grey matter volume between heavy cannabis users (n=33) and matched controls (n=42). The paper reports voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts (whole-brain analysis with a priori ROI masks and thresholds for whole-brain findings) and within-group voxelwise regressions relating GM volume to cannabis use measures. Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance class: alcohol) to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and regression) with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (e.g., superior temporal gyrus) and provides participant demographics, substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/coordinates and described in text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between stimulant-dependent patients and matched healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-way ANCOVA, FWE cluster-corrected) with figures and coordinates, as well as ROI cross-validation. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is original human MRI data. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study that performed voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume differences (VBM results), including findings outside predefined ROIs (reported in Supporting Information Table S5), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Voxelwise results are provided (tables/figures) and methods report participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that directly compares adolescents with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to matched healthy controls. The manuscript reports whole-brain VBM analyses and explicitly states a main effect of group (AUD vs HC) with voxelwise results reported in tables (Table 2 and supplemental tables/figures), and describes preprocessing and statistical software (SPM8) and MRI field strength (3T). Participant demographics and substance use characteristics are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not violate exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only nor non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing active methamphetamine (stimulant) users (n=17) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (whole-brain VBM) and ROI subcortical volumetry. The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxel-wise contrasts (GMD decreases and increases) and ROI volumetric results, and provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM analyses) with family-wise error correction and provides regional results (figures and tables with coordinates). Participant characteristics (sex, drinking history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM pipeline) are described. It is not ROI-only and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users (n=20) to matched controls (n=20) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density), regional volume, and shape analyses.
